known_disagreements.leading_hide: flashmap hides the whole failing one second period, which starts before the flashing does. Under the any overlap rule that shows up as false positive windows in the calm lead-in. It is the direction a safety layer should err in, and it is counted here rather than excused: see onset_lead_windows.
known_disagreements.one_second_period_boundary: The ground truth counts flashes in a half open one second period and flashmap counts them in a closed trailing one. On a clean square wave at exactly the flash limit the closed reading finds one more flash than the half open one. Look at the flash_rate_hz error curve at 3 Hz to see what it costs. Neither reading is written in the spec.

limits: Synthetic SDR intended-signal conformance, not clinical validation or a device test. Matrix/range conversion was corrected after the archived evaluation under a logged protocol deviation. Production detector thresholds and resolution are unchanged. Encoded near-limit signals can still cross thresholds. Baselines, IRIS ground-truth cross-checks and real-clip human labeling were not completed by this run.

published.what_these_are: the same numbers as the tables below, rounded and with short keys, because eval/readme_sync.py quotes a dotted path with no spaces in it. A document quotes these.

sample.statement: All 3000 frozen clip identities were measured afresh with one recorded source tree and encoding protocol. Every exclusion is counted. Both preregistered window-overlap rules and the diagnostic tight-bounds rule use these same rows.

window_rules.baselines: the two frame based baselines have no intervals, so a flagged frame marks the window that contains it, which is the mapping EVAL_PLAN section 6 gives them. The half window rule does not apply to them and is not reported for them.
window_rules.primary: any overlap at all between a detector interval and the window
window_rules.sensitivity: at least half the window covered, reported as @half_window
